title: The Shaheedan misl
hookLine: the martyrs' misl, linked to Baba Deep Singh

lines: A VILLAGE, A LEADER, A COUNTRY, A DUTY.
cards: The misls you've met this block mostly wear a name from a map or a family tree: a village, a leader, a stretch of country. The Nishanwalias took theirs from a duty. Today's band called itself after the dead.
Not after a defeat, and not exactly after a grief: after the people who had given their lives, whose example the riders meant to keep. Shaheed is the Punjabi word for a martyr.
This is the Shaheedan misl, the band of the martyrs.

teach.b: Sikh tradition ties this band to Baba Deep Singh.
This path has told his story: the old scholar who left his study at Damdama Sahib to defend the Harmandir and who, tradition says, fought on to reach the holy precinct even after a mortal wound.
The Shaheedan misl is remembered as the band that grew from those around him, keeping his name and his place alive.

teach.h: A NAME TELLS RIDERS WHO THEY ARE.
teach.b: A name tells riders who they are before anyone gives an order. A band called after a village rides for that village.
A band called after martyrs rides with them, in a sense: every time someone said the name, the dead were in the room. Then the center.

Tradition links the band to Damdama Sahib, where Baba Deep Singh had worked with the scripture. A band named for those who died for the faith kept close to the place where the faith was copied, read and taught.
Sword and book in the same hands, a pairing Sikh tradition holds dear. The hardest part: a name like this could become a boast. Sikh memory doesn't treat martyrdom as a prize to chase.
In Ardas, the daily prayer, Sikhs remember those who gave their heads and did not give up their faith, and they ask for the same steadiness, not for a death.
The martyrs are remembered so the living can stand straight.

how: In Ardas, the prayer said at the close of Sikh services, Sikhs remember the martyrs who held to their faith; Baba Deep Singh is remembered at gurdwaras in Amritsar and at Damdama Sahib.

o: a scholar who copies and guards the scripture
a warrior who rides into battle seeking death
a martyr, one who gave their life for the faith

games.q: you're naming a new band of riders. you could name it for your village, for your leader, or for something else. what does this band choose?
o: the martyrs whose example it means to keep.
games.why: it became the Shaheedan misl, the band of the martyrs, linked by tradition to Baba Deep Singh.

practice: Bring to mind someone who gave up something real for others: a figure from history, or someone close, a parent who worked nights, a friend who took the blame, someone who stayed when leaving was easier.
Hold their face or their name, nothing grand, and let what they gave be seen for a moment; if you pray, let Waheguru ride each breath out as you remember them.

wordCard.voice: shaheed, the Punjabi word for a martyr, that named the Shaheedan misl, linked by tradition to Baba Deep Singh and to Damdama Sahib, the place of study. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: shaheed, a martyr. The Shaheedan are the martyrs.

carryVoice: Your line: the martyrs' band. Remembered, never chased. Day eight hundred ninety-eight, done.
